map.Ignoring risk completely and hoping noth: Deciding to skip a risky activity to avoid the loss
map.Borrowing at high interest to pay for ev: Paying premiums to an insurer that covers large losses
map.Buying a full policy for every risk, how: Installing smoke alarms to lower the chance of a fire

ww.Deciding to skip a risky activity to avo: Skipping a risky activity is risk avoidance, not self-insuring, which means setting aside your own money to pay for losses that do happen.
ww.Paying premiums to an insurer that cover: Paying premiums shifts the loss to an insurance company, which is risk transfer; self-insuring means keeping the risk and paying from your own savings.
ww.Installing smoke alarms to lower the cha: Smoke alarms reduce how likely a loss is, which is risk reduction; self-insuring means saving money to pay for a loss yourself.

map.The bookstore at $13.50, because tips ar: The bookstore at $13.50, since its tips raise the rate
map.The bookstore at $12 plus extra benefits: The cafe at $16.50, because $15 plus $1.50 in tips

ww.The bookstore at $13.50, since its tips: The bookstore total of $13.50 is still below the cafe's $15 per hour, so higher tips do not make the bookstore pay more.
The $1.50 tip average belongs to the bookstore job, not the cafe, so the cafe pays $15 per hour while the bookstore averages $13.50.

map.A job with no pay for the worker at all: A job done without pay to help a charity
map.A job for only one day a year, like a ho: A job held by a worker younger than 18

ww.A job done without pay to help a charity: Unpaid work for a charity is volunteering; a part-time job pays wages but involves fewer weekly hours than a full-time job.
ww.A job held by a worker younger than 18: A part-time job is defined by working fewer hours than full time, not by the worker's age, since adults and teens can both work part time.

map.Plans have no cost, so the choice is nev: A plan is a need if most of your friends have the same one
map.Every plan is a want, so none of them ca: Plans are wants since people lived without phones in the past
map.Every plan is a need at any price, since: The most expensive plan is the need because it works best

ww.A plan is a need if most of your friends: Whether friends have a plan does not make it a need; a need is something necessary, such as basic service for communication, work, or safety.
ww.Plans are wants since people lived witho: Basic phone service is often essential today for work, school, and safety, so some plans count as needs while premium extras are wants.
ww.The most expensive plan is the need beca: Price and extra features do not make something a need; a basic plan can meet essential communication, while premium extras are wants.

map.Always better value than anything else: Usually a lower price because items are sold in bulk
map.Always lower than all other options: About the same price as making it yourself
map.Free of any fees or extra charges at all: A tax added to purchases made on weekends

ww.Usually a lower price because items are: Convenience items such as pre-cut food or delivery usually cost more per item, not less, since buyers pay extra for saved time.
ww.About the same price as making it yourse: Convenience products typically cost more than doing the work yourself, so the price is not about the same; the premium pays for saved time.
ww.A tax added to purchases made on weekend: No special weekend tax exists for convenience purchases; the extra cost is a higher price or fee that pays for saved time and effort.

map.Yes always, because coupons are free mon: Yes, because the $4 item becomes free after the $10 coupon
map.No, because coupons never work in any st: No, because the coupon would raise her total to $54

ww.Yes, because the $4 item becomes free af: The $10 coupon lowers the whole $50 total to $40, so the $4 item is not free; she saves $6 compared with paying $46.
ww.No, because the coupon would raise her t: The coupon subtracts $10 from $50, giving $40, which is less than $46, so the total goes down rather than up to $54.

map.It removes the need for any bank account: It raises the interest rate paid on the account
map.It increases fees on your savings accoun: It earns a bonus from the government each month

ww.It raises the interest rate paid on the: Automatic transfers move money on a schedule but do not change the interest rate, which is set by the account terms.
ww.It earns a bonus from the government eac: Automatic transfers simply move your own money into savings; the government does not pay a bonus for using them.

map.Investing is for spending only, while sa: Saving is for long-term growth while investing is for short-term needs
map.Saving has more risk than investing alwa: Saving earns higher returns than investing over the long run

ww.Saving is for long-term growth while inv: This reverses the two ideas: saving keeps money safe and easy to reach for short-term needs, while investing aims for growth over the long term.
ww.Saving earns higher returns than investi: Investing in assets like stocks has historically earned higher returns than savings accounts over long periods, though with more risk.

map.Buying one stock only, which gives the b: Choosing the stock with the highest price
map.Selling everything you own and holding o: Timing purchases to buy when prices are lowest

ww.Choosing the stock with the highest pric: Asset allocation is about spreading money across asset classes, not picking the highest priced stock, since price per share says nothing about quality.
ww.Timing purchases to buy when prices are: Buying at low prices is market timing; asset allocation is deciding how much to hold in stocks, bonds, and cash to match risk and goals.

map.They guarantee profits for every single: They are insured by the FDIC against losses
map.They never change in value over the long: They pay a fixed interest rate set by the fund

ww.They are insured by the FDIC against los: The FDIC insures bank deposits, not investments; index funds can lose value when the market falls and have no federal loss protection.
ww.They pay a fixed interest rate set by th: Index funds follow a market index, so their value and returns rise and fall with the market instead of paying a fixed rate.

map.It guarantees dividends for every stock: It means the company will start paying dividends soon
map.Past gains always repeat, so a rising st: The broker must refund you if the price falls later

ww.It means the company will start paying d: A price rise says nothing about dividends; many fast-rising companies pay none, and the past gain does not predict future payouts.
ww.The broker must refund you if the price: Brokers do not refund losses when prices fall; buying after a rise is a risk you accept, and past gains do not protect you.

map.You pay no interest at all ever: Interest stops once you make a payment
map.The debt disappears in a year or so: The balance is paid off within a few months

ww.Interest stops once you make a payment: Interest keeps building on the unpaid balance after a payment, so paying just the minimum leaves a balance that continues to grow with interest.
ww.The balance is paid off within a few mon: Minimum payments are small and mostly cover interest, so the balance usually takes years to pay off rather than a few months.

map.A loan with no interest to pay at all: A loan that charges a one-time fee instead of interest
map.A loan that has no payments to make at a: A loan secured by a car or house you own

ww.A loan that charges a one-time fee inste: A fixed-rate loan still charges interest; the rate simply stays the same through the term instead of replacing interest with a fee.
ww.A loan secured by a car or house you own: A loan backed by collateral is a secured loan, which describes security, not whether the interest rate stays fixed or changes.

map.Ten times income always, whatever their: Ten times their income to match a rule of thumb
map.A policy for every pet that they own at: A large policy sized to a future spouse's needs

ww.Ten times their income to match a rule o: A multiple-of-income rule suits people with dependents; someone with no dependents and few debts would pay premiums for coverage nobody needs.
ww.A large policy sized to a future spouse': Life insurance should cover current dependents and debts; planning for a spouse who does not exist wastes premium money for this person.

map.To avoid hiring anyone for the open posi: To check the candidate's credit score and bank balance
map.To test the candidate's typing speed onl: To collect the candidate's tax forms for payroll

ww.To check the candidate's credit score an: Employers interview to judge skills and fit; a candidate's bank balance is private and not a hiring measure, and credit checks are separate.
ww.To collect the candidate's tax forms for: Tax forms are collected after someone is hired; an interview is meant to judge whether the candidate fits the job and team.

map.Compare only the total price: Compare the brand names on each label
map.Choose the smaller package always: Compare the size of each package
map.Choose the bigger package always: Compare the expiration dates on each

ww.Compare the brand names on each label: Brand names do not show which product costs less for the amount you get; unit price puts different sizes on equal footing.
ww.Compare the size of each package: Package size alone does not show value; the larger one may cost more per ounce, so you need price divided by amount.
ww.Compare the expiration dates on each: Expiration dates matter for freshness but do not show which product costs less; unit price compares cost fairly across sizes.

map.The price of the game only, not what you: The $50 sticker price shown on the game's box
map.The sales tax only, not the price of the: The amount of sales tax added at the register

ww.The $50 sticker price shown on the game': The price is the money cost, but opportunity cost is the value of the next best thing you give up by spending it.
ww.The amount of sales tax added at the reg: Sales tax is part of what you pay, but opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative use of the money, not a tax amount.

map.Buy two of every item that is marked dow: Buy items with the biggest percent discount first
map.Buy anything marked down, whether or not: Buy it if the sale ends within the next few hours

ww.Buy items with the biggest percent disco: A big discount does not make an unplanned item worth buying; a good rule is to buy just what was already planned.
ww.Buy it if the sale ends within the next: Time pressure is a sales tactic; a deadline does not make an unplanned purchase a good idea, and it can cause impulse buying.

map.They always pay no interest, as credit u: They pay stockholders a share of the profits
map.They never insure deposits of any member: Membership is open to the public with no eligibility rules
map.They are not regulated by any government: They are run by the Federal Reserve for local members

ww.They pay stockholders a share of the pro: Credit unions are owned by their members, not outside stockholders, so earnings go back to members as better rates and lower fees.
ww.Membership is open to the public with no: Credit unions require membership based on a common bond such as employer, location, or group, so they are not open without eligibility rules.
ww.They are run by the Federal Reserve for: Credit unions are member-owned cooperatives supervised by the NCUA; the Federal Reserve does not operate them.

map.Tips always lead to profit for every inv: Tips are checked by regulators before they are posted
map.Tips are always guaranteed by regulators: Tips cost money to read and the fees reduce your returns

ww.Tips are checked by regulators before th: Regulators do not review social media posts before they appear, so tips can be false, hyped, or scams with no prior vetting.
ww.Tips cost money to read and the fees red: Most social media tips are free to read; the real risk is that they may be wrong, biased, or scams, not a fee for reading them.

map.Old accounts always cost money to keep o: Old accounts are removed from your report after one year
map.They reduce your score always, by a lot: Open accounts make lenders see you as a higher risk

ww.Old accounts are removed from your repor: Closed or open accounts stay on a credit report for years, so old accounts keep adding to your credit history length.
ww.Open accounts make lenders see you as a: Lenders view a long record of well-managed accounts as lower risk, so keeping old accounts open generally helps your credit.

map.Only if the item is stolen from the shop: Yes, because it lets you return the item if you change your mind
map.Always, because warranties are free of c: Yes, because a $20 cost is small next to future repair bills
map.Always, because the item always fails an: Yes, because most $30 items break within the first week

ww.Yes, because it lets you return the item: An extended warranty covers repairs or breakdowns, not buyer's regret; return policies are separate, and $20 is high for a $30 item.
ww.Yes, because a $20 cost is small next to: A $20 warranty on a $30 item costs two thirds of its price, which is large compared with the item, so the value is poor.
ww.Yes, because most $30 items break within: Most inexpensive items work for much longer than a week, and replacing a $30 item costs less than the $20 warranty.

map.Coverage for rain damage only, paid in s: Flood coverage for a home in a storm zone
map.Coverage for pets only, not for people o: Health coverage for the policyholder's family

ww.Flood coverage for a home in a storm zon: Flood damage needs its own policy; an umbrella policy adds liability limits and does not cover damage to your property.
ww.Health coverage for the policyholder's f: Health costs are covered by health insurance; an umbrella policy provides extra liability protection against lawsuits and large judgments.

map.Benefits are always worthless to workers: Benefits are taxed at a higher rate than regular wages
map.Pay is the only factor ever worth thinki: A job's title matters more than pay or benefits

ww.Benefits are taxed at a higher rate than: Many benefits, such as employer health insurance, are tax advantaged and add value, so lower pay with strong benefits can be a good choice.
ww.A job's title matters more than pay or b: A title does not pay bills or protect against costs; total pay, benefits, and growth opportunities matter more when comparing jobs.

map.It guarantees promotions, as each new em: It shows employers you are loyal to one company
map.It has no effect on how employers see yo: It makes employers view your resume as more experienced
map.It always raises pay at every new job th: It usually cuts your pay at each new employer

ww.It shows employers you are loyal to one: Moving often does the opposite of showing loyalty; employers may see short stays as a sign you might leave quickly.
ww.It makes employers view your resume as m: Short stints can raise questions about commitment instead of adding experience, so employers may see the pattern as a concern.
ww.It usually cuts your pay at each new emp: Job changes often bring raises, so pay does not typically fall; the main concern for employers is stability, not salary.

map.They are interest-free forever and ever: They require a large down payment to open
map.They always charge no fees of any kind: They can be used anywhere that takes credit cards

ww.They require a large down payment to ope: Store cards do not need a down payment; the drawback is that they often have high interest rates that make carried balances costly.
ww.They can be used anywhere that takes cre: Many store cards work just at that retailer, and the larger drawback is high interest rates on balances you carry.

map.Skip savings and spend all of your pay f: Treat yourself to a purchase right after payday
map.Spend before saving anything at all from: Pay off your smallest debt before saving anything
map.Pay bills last, after all of your spendi: Pay bills early and save what is left over

ww.Treat yourself to a purchase right after: Spending on a treat first is the opposite of paying yourself first, which moves money into savings before other spending.
ww.Pay off your smallest debt before saving: Paying yourself first means setting aside savings from each paycheck as the first step, not paying debts before saving.
ww.Pay bills early and save what is left ov: Saving what is left over puts savings last; paying yourself first sets aside savings right away before other spending.

map.A trendy jacket that is worn only once: A trendy jacket bought for this season's style
map.No jacket at all, just a thin summer shi: A designer jacket chosen mainly for its brand name

ww.A trendy jacket bought for this season's: A jacket chosen for a passing trend is likely to be worn briefly, which raises its cost per use compared with a durable one.
ww.A designer jacket chosen mainly for its: Paying extra for a brand name does not lower cost per use; durability and many wears do, so this choice is poor value.

map.Time guarantees profit on any investment: Time turns risky investments into safe ones
map.Markets never fall in value over the who: Dividends make up for losses in the stock price

ww.Time turns risky investments into safe o: Holding longer does not remove risk; a long time frame just gives markets more chances to recover from downturns.
ww.Dividends make up for losses in the stoc: Dividends may soften losses but do not make up for them, and many stocks pay none; recovery comes from markets rising over time.

map.Using 90% of the limit every month: Using about half of your available credit
map.Maxing out every card that you own: Using about 70% of the limit each month
map.Using 100% of the limit every month: Keeping a balance near 60% of each limit

ww.Using about half of your available credi: Half of your limit is well above the 30 percent guideline and can lower a credit score; lower utilization looks more responsible.
ww.Using about 70% of the limit each month: Utilization near 70 percent is high and signals risk to lenders; the common advice is to keep balances below 30 percent.
ww.Keeping a balance near 60% of each limit: A balance near 60 percent of a limit is above the recommended 30 percent and can pull a credit score down.

map.Debits always exceed credits: Revenue equals expenses in the period

ww.Each entry must involve cash: Not every transaction involves cash; double-entry requires that total debits equal total credits, whatever accounts are used.
ww.Revenue equals expenses in the period: Revenue and expenses do not need to match; a business can earn a profit or loss, and just debits and credits must balance.

map.Reporting expenses that never happened: Moving income into a personal account to hide it
map.Not filing a return at all for the year: Paying employees in cash without recording it

ww.Moving income into a personal account to: Hiding income by moving it is tax evasion, which is illegal; legal tax reduction uses deductions and credits the law allows.
ww.Paying employees in cash without recordi: Paying staff off the books hides expenses and payroll taxes, which is illegal; legal reduction means claiming allowed deductions.

ww.Assets equal liabilities alone: Assets equal liabilities plus owner's equity, so leaving out equity breaks the accounting equation unless equity is zero.
ww.Cash must increase or decrease: Many transactions leave cash unchanged, such as buying supplies on credit; the equation stays balanced whatever accounts change.

map.The difference is always an odd number: The difference is a multiple of 10
map.The difference is always exactly $1: The difference is twice the largest entry

ww.The difference is a multiple of 10: Swapping two digits changes a number by a multiple of 9, not 10, so a difference divisible by 9 hints at the error.
ww.The difference is twice the largest entr: A transposition changes a figure by a multiple of 9, so the gap is unrelated to doubling the largest entry.

map.An account that is always zero or negati: An account that holds the owner's personal funds
map.An account used only by the auditors: An account that records unpaid supplier bills
map.An account for owner withdrawals only: An account that closes out each period

ww.An account that holds the owner's person: Personal funds belong in a drawing or capital account; a contra account offsets a related account with an opposite normal balance.
ww.An account that records unpaid supplier: Unpaid supplier bills belong in Accounts Payable, a liability; a contra account offsets another account instead.
ww.An account that closes out each period: Closing temporary accounts is a separate idea; a contra account sits beside a related account and reduces its balance, like Accumulated Depreciation.

ww.Revenue and expense accounts: Revenue and expense accounts are temporary and are closed to zero, so they do not show balances on the post-closing trial balance.
ww.Adjusting entries for the period: Adjusting entries are made before closing and appear in the worksheet and journal; the post-closing trial balance lists permanent account balances.
ww.Drawing and income summary accounts: Drawing and income summary are temporary accounts closed to zero, so they do not appear with balances after closing.

map.Only profitable periods are ever reporte: Income is reported when the owner decides
map.A business reports only once, at closing: Results are reported when the business is sold
map.Periods must always be exactly one year: Reports cover periods of different lengths each time

ww.Income is reported when the owner decide: Reporting depends on regular periods, not on the owner's wish, which would make results hard to compare between periods.
ww.Results are reported when the business i: Reports are prepared at regular intervals during operation so owners and lenders get timely information, not just at a sale.
ww.Reports cover periods of different lengt: The concept uses equal periods so results can be compared; unequal periods would distort comparisons of income between periods.

ww.Department managers and supervisors: Managers and supervisors work inside the company and use detailed internal reports, which makes them internal users.
ww.The company's own sales staff: Sales staff are employees of the company and are internal users; external users are outside parties like investors and lenders.
ww.In-house accounting clerks: Accounting clerks work for the company and use its records daily, so they are internal users rather than external ones.

ww.The company's outside tax preparers: Outside tax preparers help with tax returns but are not responsible for certifying financial reports; SOX puts this duty on top company officers.
ww.The company's human resources director: The HR director manages people, not financial reports; SOX Section 302 requires the CEO and CFO to certify accuracy.

map.Always choosing the lowest numbers: Choosing the numbers that favor the firm
map.Agreeing with the client at all times: Following the client's wishes on reports

ww.Choosing the numbers that favor the firm: Picking figures that favor the firm is bias; objectivity requires fair, impartial reporting without leaning toward one party.
ww.Following the client's wishes on reports: Following a client's wishes can compromise independence; objectivity means making fair judgments even when the client disagrees.

map.Naming every customer in the financial n: Listing each employee's pay in the notes
map.Reporting only the profitable results of: Reporting the numbers the managers prefer

ww.Listing each employee's pay in the notes: Individual pay is private and not needed by most users; disclosure covers information that is relevant to decisions.
ww.Reporting the numbers the managers prefe: Disclosure is based on what users need to know, not on what managers prefer; picking results would mislead statement users.

map.External auditors work only for the comp: External auditors are company staff; internal ones are outside firms
map.Internal auditors work for the IRS and t: Internal auditors check tax returns; external ones check payroll

ww.External auditors are company staff; int: This reverses the roles: internal auditors are company employees, while external auditors are independent outsiders who give an opinion on the statements.
ww.Internal auditors check tax returns; ext: Internal auditors review controls and operations for management, and external auditors give an opinion on financial statements; neither is defined by tax or payroll checks.

map.Paying taxes late on purpose every singl: Delaying payment to earn interest on the money
map.Refusing to file a return at all this ye: Filing the return under a different name

ww.Delaying payment to earn interest on the: Paying late brings penalties and interest from the tax agency; avoidance means legally reducing the tax owed through allowed methods.
ww.Filing the return under a different name: Using a false name is fraud and illegal; avoidance lowers tax through deductions and credits the law allows.

map.Only the oldest partner is taxed on it: It is taxed at the corporate rate
map.It is not taxed at all by any government: It is taxed once the partnership is sold

ww.It is taxed at the corporate rate: A partnership is not taxed like a corporation; income passes through to the partners and is taxed on their personal returns.
ww.It is taxed once the partnership is sold: Partnership income is taxed each year as it is earned and passed to partners, not delayed until the business is sold.

map.A corporation that pays no taxes ever at: A corporation taxed twice at higher rates
map.A corporation owned only by the governme: A corporation that sells shares on exchanges

ww.A corporation taxed twice at higher rate: Double taxation applies to C corporations; an S corporation passes income to owners and generally avoids a separate corporate tax.
ww.A corporation that sells shares on excha: An S corporation is limited in the number and type of shareholders and cannot be publicly traded; its defining feature is pass-through taxation.

map.Tax depreciation is never allowed by law: Tax depreciation must follow the book amount
map.They must always be identical in amount: Tax depreciation is recorded after an asset is sold

ww.Tax depreciation must follow the book am: Tax depreciation follows IRS rules such as MACRS, so it does not have to match the book amount, which follows GAAP.
ww.Tax depreciation is recorded after an as: Tax depreciation is deducted over the years an asset is used, not after it is sold; book and tax amounts can differ.

map.Only the return itself: A copy of last year's return

ww.A summary of estimated amounts: Estimates do not prove a deduction; the IRS expects receipts and documents that support each amount claimed.
ww.A copy of last year's return: Last year's return does not support this year's deductions; the taxpayer needs receipts and records for the current figures.

map.Software that works only on paper: Software for recording sales by hand
map.Software that only works when offline: Software saved on a USB flash drive

ww.Software for recording sales by hand: Cloud-based software is a computer program used over the internet, not a method of hand recording sales.
ww.Software saved on a USB flash drive: Software on a flash drive is stored locally, while cloud software runs on remote servers and is reached through the internet.

map.Bookkeepers always earn more than accoun: Bookkeepers give tax advice; accountants record entries
map.Accountants only enter receipts into the: Both must hold a CPA license to work
map.There is no difference between them at a: Bookkeepers audit statements for outside investors

ww.Bookkeepers give tax advice; accountants: This reverses their roles: bookkeepers record transactions, while accountants analyze data and give tax and financial advice.
ww.Both must hold a CPA license to work: Bookkeepers do not need a CPA license, and not all accountants hold one; the roles differ in scope and training.
ww.Bookkeepers audit statements for outside: Auditing statements is accountant or auditor work; bookkeepers record daily transactions in the books.

map.Laws never change over the long years: Tax law is set once by the IRS
map.Only clients need to know the rules: Tax software handles the rules for them
map.It affects only large companies and owne: Changes apply to corporations, not to individuals

ww.Tax law is set once by the IRS: Tax law is changed often through legislation, rulings, and court cases, so accountants must keep learning to stay current.
ww.Tax software handles the rules for them: Software can help with calculations, but accountants must know current law to advise clients and spot errors.
ww.Changes apply to corporations, not to in: Tax changes affect individuals, small businesses, and large companies, so accountants who serve clients of all types must follow them.

map.Learning only when forced to by a boss o: Learning a new skill when a job ends
map.Memorizing one set of rules forever and: Mastering the rules once and relying on them

ww.Learning a new skill when a job ends: Lifelong learning is a steady habit of updating skills throughout a career, not something done just after a job ends.
ww.Mastering the rules once and relying on: Rules, standards, and software change, so relying on one mastered set becomes outdated; lifelong learning means continuing to update.

map.Money is the only thing that matters to: Prices must be adjusted for inflation in the records
map.Every item must be recorded at its curre: Business and personal records must be kept in separate books

ww.Prices must be adjusted for inflation in: The assumption treats the dollar as a stable unit, so records are not adjusted for inflation; it says activity can be recorded in money.
ww.Business and personal records must be ke: Keeping business and personal records apart is the business entity concept, not the monetary unit assumption.

map.After every single sale that is made in: Each time a new shipment is received from suppliers
map.Only when the owner decides, whenever it: Whenever the owner feels the stock is getting low
map.Never, because no physical count is made: At the start of the period before sales occur

ww.Each time a new shipment is received fro: Updating with each shipment and sale describes the perpetual system; the periodic system updates inventory after a physical count.
ww.Whenever the owner feels the stock is ge: Records follow a set accounting method, not the owner's feelings; the periodic system updates inventory after a count at period end.
ww.At the start of the period before sales: Periodic inventory is updated after a count at the end of the period, not at the start before sales happen.

map.A system that ignores purchases and only: A system that estimates inventory from sales totals
map.A system that updates inventory records: A system that updates inventory records at the end of each period
map.A system that records only cash sales ma: A system that values inventory at its expected selling price

ww.A system that estimates inventory from s: Estimating from sales is not the perpetual system, which tracks each purchase and sale directly in the records.
ww.A system that updates inventory records: Updating at period end after a count describes the periodic system, which is the opposite of perpetual.
ww.A system that values inventory at its ex: Perpetual systems track units and costs as they move; valuing at expected selling price is a different valuation idea.

map.Receivables are shown only in cash form: Receivables are shown at the full invoiced amount
map.Receivables are removed entirely from th: Receivables are shown with expected gains added

ww.Receivables are shown at the full invoic: The allowance method reduces receivables for expected losses, so they are not shown at the full invoiced amount.
ww.Receivables are shown with expected gain: The allowance method subtracts expected losses from receivables; it does not add gains to them.

map.Recording revenue only at year end, once: Recording revenue when the customer's payment clears the bank
map.Recording revenue when the order is firs: Recording revenue when the sales team signs a price quote

ww.Recording revenue when the customer's pa: Waiting for payment describes cash-basis timing; the five-step model recognizes revenue when control of goods or services transfers.
ww.Recording revenue when the sales team si: A price quote is just a proposal and transfers nothing to the customer, so no revenue has yet been earned.

map.No record of invoices kept anywhere at a: Higher costs from retyping each invoice
map.Slower payments from every single custom: More data entry work for the staff

ww.Higher costs from retyping each invoice: Automation removes retyping, which lowers costs and errors; manual re-entry is a feature of non-automated invoicing.
ww.More data entry work for the staff: Automated invoicing reduces data entry by creating invoices from existing records, so staff do less of it.

map.Recording only when cash changes hands,: Recording income when cash is received and expenses when paid
map.Recording only expenses and never any re: Recording expenses when paid and revenue when ordered

ww.Recording income when cash is received a: That is cash-basis accounting; accrual records revenue when earned and expenses when incurred, whatever the cash timing.
ww.Recording expenses when paid and revenue: Accrual records expenses when incurred and revenue when earned, not when paid or ordered, so this mixes the two methods.

map.An account used only for revenue items a: An account with a debit balance that records sales
map.An account that is always zero or has no: An account with a credit balance that records owner investments

ww.An account with a debit balance that rec: Sales are recorded in revenue accounts with credit balances; a contra-asset has a credit balance and reduces an asset.
ww.An account with a credit balance that re: Owner investments are recorded in a capital account within equity; a contra-asset reduces an asset's value.

ww.Revenue and expense accounts: Revenue and expense accounts are temporary and closed to zero, so they do not appear with balances after closing.
ww.Adjusting entries from the period: Adjusting entries are made before closing; the post-closing trial balance lists just the balances left in permanent accounts.
ww.Income summary and drawing accounts: Income summary and drawing are temporary accounts closed to zero, so they do not appear with balances.

map.Record assets at current market value on: Record assets at their expected resale price
map.Do not record assets that the firm owns: Record assets at the tax assessor's value

ww.Record assets at their expected resale p: The cost principle uses what was paid, which can be verified, not a guessed future resale price.
ww.Record assets at the tax assessor's valu: The assessor's value is an outside opinion; the cost principle records assets at the actual purchase price paid.

map.Software requires paper only, so records: Records are lost when the office loses power
map.Data can never be backed up in the cloud: Software updates must be installed by hand at each office
